identified_discrete_force_choice.interpretation: The product-form capillary source is not generally a pure production pressure gradient when mu_h varies spatially. The measured residual is split algebraically into the diagnostic -phi G_h(mu_h) term and E_h. checks.expectation: phi=1 inside (liquid), phi=0 outside (gas); dphi/dr<0; n_out=-grad(phi)/|grad(phi)| = +r_hat
checks.name: phi_orientation_and_normal

checks.expectation: mu = +dF/dphi (directional derivative); mu>0 at a convex liquid interface; int mu dphi = sigma_e/R
checks.name: chemical_potential_sign

checks.expectation: net capillary force at a convex liquid interface points toward the liquid: int F.n_out dr < 0
checks.name: korteweg_force_direction

checks.expectation: F = +grad(psi) is balanced by grad(P) with P = +psi (momentum carries -grad(P))
checks.name: pressure_gradient_convention

checks.expectation: pressure_field() is the projection pressure of step(): u* - dt grad(P) is divergence free
checks.name: diagnostic_equals_projection

checks.expectation: delta_p = P_liquid - P_gas > 0 and delta_p R We ~ +1 (probes: liquid core, far gas)
checks.name: laplace_jump_sign_and_scale

checks.expectation: the force integral -int F_r dr and the projection-pressure jump are the same quantity (catches any compensating sign in the diagnostic)
checks.name: force_integral_matches_projection_jump

checks.expectation: flow driven by the capillary force lowers F: -dF/dt = int mu u.grad(phi) > 0 (cos(mu grad phi, u) > 0)
checks.name: free_energy_consistency

checks.expectation: Form A (+mu grad phi) and Form B (-phi grad mu) drive the same flow (cos ~ +1); the solver force belongs to that class, not to its negative
checks.name: force_form_equivalence_class
checks.note: Form A and Form B differ by grad(mu phi) only in the continuum; on the grid the difference is O((dx/eps)^2).

checks.expectation: informational: for uniform (relaxed) mu Form A keeps delta_p R We = +1, Form B loses it (reduced pressure)
checks.name: relaxed_mu_form_choice
checks.note: Form A is retained: its projection pressure is the mechanical pressure whose jump is the Young-Laplace value for any admissible mu; this is a design argument, not a benchmark fit.

conventions.chemical_potential: mu = dF/dphi = f'(phi)/eps - eps lap(phi); mu = +eps |dphi/dr| / r > 0 at a convex liquid interface
conventions.grad_phi_direction: dphi/dr < 0 across the interface: grad(phi) points gas -> liquid (outside -> inside)
conventions.korteweg_force: F_cap = +(SIGMA_NORM/We) mu grad(phi) / rho_l  ~  -(SIGMA_NORM/We) phi grad(mu) / rho_l (up to a pure gradient); F . n_out < 0 (toward the liquid / centre of curvature)
conventions.laplace_jump: delta_p = P_liquid - P_gas = +sigma/R = +1/(We R); laplace_ratio = delta_p R We -> +1 (2-D)
conventions.phase_orientation: phi = 1 liquid, phi = 0 gas; phi(r) = 0.5 (1 - tanh((r - R) / (sqrt(2) eps)))
conventions.pressure_gradient: du/dt = ... - grad(P) + F; u+ = u* - dt grad(P), lap(P) = div(u*)/dt; static balance grad(P) = F
